earlier_scan.source_named: SIL PNG bibliography for Doga (dgg, via the Internet Archive) lists only sociolinguistic works (Landweer 2006, 2010); no phonology or grammar of Doga located.

sources.citation: Landweer, M. Lynn. 2010. Land-language link. In K. A. McElhanon & G. Reesink (eds.), A mosaic of languages and cultures: studies celebrating the career of Karl J. Franklin, 351-380. SIL e-Books 19. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic study of Gabobora (Anuki) vs Doga vitality, migration, marriage; zero hits for stress/accent/phonology/syllable in the chapter.

sources.citation: Svensson 2006, Are Organised Phonology Data (sister language Are [mwc], held)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checked only for mention of Doga: none. Describes Are, not Doga; not used.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988) (also lendable online at archive.org)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Doga appears only in the Are-Taupota chain tree and in cognate sets / consonant correspondences (ch. 3 and 6); Doga data credited to 'Dutton n.d.'. No stress remark for Doga.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Strong 1911). Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology. No grammar, sketch or phonology of Doga is known to Glottolog.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Doga / dgg / Magabara wordlist in ABVD.

sources.citation: OLAC resources for dgg (2025-11-03); PARADISEC items TD1-P108 (Dutton 1968, Doga audio) and AC2-OLVOC403 (Capell, Numerals and affixes for seven Oceanic languages, 2-page ms); Endangered Languages Project entry 2147
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalogue records only: no language description exists in OLAC for Doga beyond Glottolog/Ethnologue entries; primary material is a 1968 Dutton tape and a 2-page Capell numerals/affixes ms.

sources.citation: Ethnologue 22nd ed. (2019), entry Doga [dgg] (the Internet Archive 2019-10-16)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Alternate name Magabara; 200 speakers (Wurm 2000); 'Dialects: None known. Lexical similarity 47%-55% with Are [mwc]'; Writing: 'Unwritten'. No phonology.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives, search filtered to dgg (the Internet Archive 2015-09-18); SIL archive records 9905 (Landweer 2006 PhD, Essex, 2 vols, not online), 9285 (Landweer 2010), 50736 (Landweer 2011)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only 3 items for Doga, all sociolinguistic (Landweer 2006, 2010, 2011). No phonology, grammar or OPD listed.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 441-523. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 21 p. 454 lists Doga villages (Magavara, Divediveni, Karuasi, Boririte) and says 'I have no dialect data on this or the next three languages in the Cape Vogel area'. Sec. 84 STRESS p. 475 is a Papuan Tip Cluster-wide remark only: stress 'seems' predictable within kinship nouns and verbs, moving one syllable toward the end when a suffix is added; stress phonemic in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima; Doga is not named.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1971. Languages of South-East Papua: a preliminary report. In Dutton, Voorhoeve & Wurm, Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14, 1-46. Pacific Linguistics A-28. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.2 Doga p. 8: unclassified, 'clearly Austronesian'; 162-item wordlist collected 23.9.69 at Karuasi (tape P108). No phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. n.d. Numerals and affixes for seven Oceanic languages: Arifama, Raga, Bubir, Maisin, Doga, Gagara, Wowonga. 2-page manuscript, PARADISEC AC2-OLVOC403.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only other archived primary Doga material; 2 pages of numerals and affixes, almost certainly silent on stress.

sources.citation: Landweer, M. Lynn. 2006. A Melanesian perspective on mechanisms of language maintenance and shift: case studies from Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, University of Essex, 2 vols.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only book-length work with Doga as a subject; the two-volume format may include an appendix with Doga wordlist/orthography or a phonological sketch, though the topic is sociolinguistic. SIL archive record 9905 says not available online.

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1968. RabaRaba Sub-D, tape TD1-P108, side 1: Doga (Karuasi), 162-item wordlist. PARADISEC.

sources.note: The only known audio of Doga (the source of Dutton 1971 and Ross 1988 Doga data); stress could in principle be heard from the recording, but no written description accompanies it.
